<STRUCT_0001>
This chapter is the first in a series of chapter on the <ACCENT_0001>tale cohomology
of schemes. In this chapter we discuss the very basics of the <ACCENT_0002>tale
topology and cohomology of abelian sheaves in this topology. Many of the
topics discussed may be safely skipped on a first reading; please see
the advice in the next section as to how to decide what to skip.

<TEXTOPEN_0001>Which sections to skip on a first reading?<TEXTCLOSE_0001>
<LOCKED_0001>

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
The initial version of this chapter was formed by the notes
of the first part of a course on <ACCENT_0001>tale cohomology taught by Johan de Jong
at Columbia University in the Fall of 2009. The original note takers were
Thibaut Pugin, Zachary Maddock and Min Lee. The second part of the
course can be found in the chapter on the trace formula, see
The Trace Formula, Section <REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0001>
We want to use the material in this chapter for the development of
theory related to algebraic spaces, Deligne-Mumford stacks, algebraic stacks,
etc. Thus we have added some pretty technical material to the original
exposition of <ACCENT_0001>tale cohomology for schemes. The reader can recognize this
material by the frequency of the word ``topos'', or by discussions related
to set theory, or by proofs dealing with very general properties of morphisms
of schemes. Some of these discussions can be skipped on a first reading.

Besides these sections there are some sporadic results that may be skipped
that the reader can recognize by the keywords given above.

<STRUCT_0001>
These lectures are about another cohomology theory. The first thing to remark
is that the Zariski topology is not entirely satisfactory. One of the main
reasons that it fails to give the results that we would want is that if <MATH_0001> is
a complex variety and <MATH_0002> is a constant sheaf then
<MATH_0003>
The reason for that is the following. In an irreducible scheme (a variety in
particular), any two nonempty open subsets meet, and so the restriction
mappings of a constant sheaf are surjective. We say that the sheaf is
<TEXTITOPEN_0001>flasque<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>. In this case, all higher <GROUPOPEN_0001><ACCENT_0001><GROUPCLOSE_0001>ech cohomology groups vanish, and
so do all higher Zariski cohomology groups. In other words, there are ``not
enough'' open sets in the Zariski topology to detect this higher cohomology.

translation:
<STRUCT_0001>
我们希望用本章的材料发展与代数空间（algebraic spaces）、Deligne-Mumford 栈（Deligne-Mumford stacks）、代数栈（algebraic stacks）等相关的理论。因此，我们在原先关于概形（schemes）的平展上同调（<ACCENT_0001>tale cohomology）的论述中加入了一些相当技术性的材料。读者可以通过“拓扑斯（topos）”一词出现的频率、与集合论（set theory）相关的讨论，或处理概形（schemes）的态射（morphisms）的非常一般的性质的证明，来辨认这些材料。初读时可以跳过其中一些讨论。

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
具体来说，我们建议读者跳过以下各节：
<STRUCT_0004>
<STRUCT_0005> 比较大（big）与小（small）的拓扑斯（topoi），第 <REF_0001> 节。
<STRUCT_0006> 恢复态射（morphisms），第 <REF_0002> 节。
<STRUCT_0007> 推送（Push）与拉回（pull），第 <REF_0003> 节。
<STRUCT_0008> 性质（Property）（A），第 <REF_0004> 节。
<STRUCT_0009> 性质（Property）（B），第 <REF_0005> 节。
<STRUCT_0010> 性质（Property）（C），第 <REF_0006> 节。
<STRUCT_0011> 小（small）平展（<ACCENT_0002>tale）位点（site）的拓扑不变性（Topological invariance），第 <REF_0007> 节。
<STRUCT_0012> 整（Integral）的普遍单射（injective）态射（morphisms），第 <REF_0008> 节。
<STRUCT_0013> 大（Big）位点（sites）与推前（pushforward），第 <REF_0009> 节。
<STRUCT_0014> 大（big）下惊叹号（lower shriek）的正合性（Exactness），第 <REF_0010> 节。
<STRUCT_0015>
除这些节以外，还有一些零散的结果可以跳过，读者可以根据上述关键词辨认这些结果。
